ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
3-day history of cough and congestion with low-grade fever and decreased oral intake

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She reports that the child has had a low-grade fever, which peaked at 38.2°C (100.8°F) yesterday. The child has been irritable and has had decreased oral intake.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
His past medical history is unremarkable, and he is up-to-date with his immunizations.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal asthma
- Paternal seasonal allergies

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: No secondhand smoke exposure. Alcohol: Not applicable. Occupation: None (infant).

VITAL SIGNS:
His respiratory rate is 50 breaths per minute, heart rate is 130 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears tachypneic and has mild intercostal retractions. Auscultation of the chest reveals diffuse wheezes and crackles bilaterally. The rest of the examination is unremarkable.

attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Difficulty breathing with chest retractions and rapid respiratory rate

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for evaluation of respiratory symptoms eight months after a prior outpatient visit for similar complaints. The parents report that the infant has had a runny nose and a mild cough for the past two days, which has progressively worsened. Today, they noticed that he is breathing rapidly and his chest seems to be retracting with each breath.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Acute bronchiolitis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal asthma
- Paternal seasonal allergies

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: No secondhand smoke exposure. Alcohol: Not applicable. Occupation: None (infant).

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, the infant is afebrile, with a respiratory rate of 60 breaths per minute, heart rate of 150 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation of 92% on room air.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Auscultation of the lungs reveals bilateral wheezing and fine crackles. The rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory Values:
- White blood cell count: 10,000/uL
- Hemoglobin: 11.5 g/dL
- Platelet count: 300,000/uL
- C-reactive protein: 2 mg/L (normal <10 mg/L)

OTHER STUDIES:
A nasopharyngeal swab is obtained for viral testing.
